History of the Equator Monument

Tugu Khatulistiwa marks the area crossed by the equator on Jalan Khatulistiwa in Batu Layang, North Pontianak. More than a photo stop, it connects geography, astronomy and the history of mapping.

Its form did not appear all at once. The present monument is the result of several marking stages that began as a geographical-survey tool in the early 20th century.

1928–1938: successive markers

Indonesia.travel describes a stake-and-arrow marker in 1928, a ring and arrow added in 1930, and a 1938 development with four belian posts.

1990–1991: protection and replica

The national tourism account describes a protective building and enlarged replica developed in 1990–1991 and inaugurated in September 1991. The earlier monument remains inside; confirm which areas are open.

Frequently asked questions

01When was the Equator Monument first built?+

The first version was installed in 1928 as a geographical-survey marker, not the visitor monument known today.

02Why did its form change several times?+

The monument developed through successive markers, then a protective building and replica inaugurated in 1991.

03Does the original marker still exist?+

The official tourism account says the earlier monument remains inside the protective building. Current room access must be confirmed with staff.
